classification.difficultyReason: Derive and factor two parameterised derivatives, use the excluded endpoints to isolate their relevant roots, and combine those roots to establish the identity.

content.prompt: Let $f(x)=x(1-x)^n$ and $g(x)=x^n(1-x)$, where $n\ne-1$. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be values on $f$ and $g$ respectively so that $f'(\alpha)=g'(\beta)=0$, where $\alpha,\beta\notin\{0,1\}$. Show that $\alpha+\beta=1$.

answer.short:
$\alpha=\dfrac{1}{n+1}$ and $\beta=\dfrac{n}{n+1}$, so $\alpha+\beta=1$.

Factor each product-rule derivative and use the non-endpoint stationary root.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=(1-x)^n-nx(1-x)^{n-1}\\f'(x)&=(1-x)^{n-1}[1-(n+1)x]\\g'(x)&=nx^{n-1}(1-x)-x^n\\g'(x)&=x^{n-1}[n-(n+1)x].\end{align*}$$

 Since $\alpha,\beta\notin\{0,1\}$ and $n\ne-1$, the stated stationary values give 

$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{1}{n+1}\\\beta&=\frac{n}{n+1}\\\alpha+\beta&=\frac{1+n}{n+1}=1.\end{align*}$$
